author: NorthEast News Desk
body: U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in August after a 0.1% increase in July, the Labor Department reported Friday. The Consumer Price Index was 3.4% higher than a year earlier, matching July’s annual rate and meeting economists’ expectations for the monthly change.

Core prices, which exclude food and energy, increased 0.3% for the month. Reuters described that as the largest rise in four months, with airline fares continuing their upward trend. The report arrived one day after firm producer-price readings and strengthened the view that underlying inflation pressure persisted despite the unchanged year-over-year headline rate.

Investors responded by increasing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise its benchmark rate at the September 15-16 policy meeting. That market pricing was a reaction recorded after the report, not a live forecast. The central bank’s target range stood at 3.50% to 3.75% when Reuters published its analysis. For households and businesses, the data reinforce the possibility that borrowing costs will remain restrictive as policymakers assess energy shocks, employment conditions and whether price increases are spreading beyond fuel-related categories.
dek: The monthly CPI increase matched expectations, while a 0.3% rise in core prices reinforced expectations of tighter Federal Reserve policy.
headline: August U.S. inflation rises 0.4% as rate-hike expectations strengthen
